To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ethanol suppresses iNOS expression in C6 glial cell by inhibiting protein binding in an octamer DNA motif located in the proximal Nos 2 promoter.
acute ethanol exposure diminishes protein occupation at the Nos2 promoter in a region containing the overlapping gamma-interferon response element/gas response element/octamer motifs.
ethanol suppresses cytokine and lipolysaccharide induction of iNOS by inhibiting protein-DNA interaction at the core promoter of the iNOS gene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that regulate iNOS expression in the brain and how alcohol modulates these mechanisms to produce a neurotoxic state.
how ethanol inhibits the inducible activity of the Nos2 (iNos) gene promoter.

the molecular mechanisms by which alcohol inhibits inducible nitrix oxide synthase (iNOS). iNOS is an enzyme that produces nitric oxide and is induced by cytokines such as interferon-gamma and bacterial products such as lipopolysacchride.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ethanol suppresses cytokine and lipopoly-saccharide induced expression of iNOS by inhibiting NF-kappaB, C/EBP, and Oct binding to their cognate motifs.
the Oct motif participates in the ethanol inhibition of cytokines and lipopolysacharide induced iN0S expression.
ethanol inhibition of iNOS expression is associated with a decrease in DNA-protein binding in the proximal promoter region, particularly at the overlapping Oct and gamma-IRE/Gas motifs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ethanol suppresses cytokine-induced iNOS activity by inhibiting the binding of transcription factor proteins to the Nos2 promoter.

ethanol inhibits the cytokine and lipopoly-saccharide induced transcription of the iNOS gene by inhibiting the binding of the Oct protein to the octamer motif in the gamma-IRE, Oct, GAS overlapping region of the Nos promoter.

the octamer motif in the gamma-IRE site of the Nos2 proximal promoter is important for cytokine and bacterial products induction of iNOS activity in glia and that acute ethanol inhibits this induction through the octamer motif.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the overlapping octamer motif in the gamma-IRE, Gas and Oct sites of the rat Nos2 promoter participates in the alcohol suppression of the cytokine/lipopolysaccharides induced activity.
ethanol may modulate the transcriptional activity of iNOS gene via the Oct motif.
the Oct motif is involved in alcohol inhibition of the rat inducible nitrite oxide synthase gene.
